spec_family.name: Exterior Fence Staining & Painting
spec_family.description: Stain and paint application for exterior wood fences (cedar, pressure-treated pine). Covers new construction AND existing fences via wood_condition dimension. Coating_type is the primary configuration dimension (transparent, semi_transparent, solid_stain, paint) — replaces quality_tier. Includes full prep (moisture verification, seasoning check for PT pine, pressure wash, mill glaze removal for cedar, chemical restoration for weathered wood), stain-blocking primer (cedar + solid/paint only), stain or paint application (spray_backbrush, brush, roll), second coat (solid_stain and paint only), final inspection, and cleanup. PaintScope delivers final SF after (LF x Height x 2) and fence_style geometric multiplier — spec does NOT compute geometry. Single paintable item (ITM_FENCE_FIELD, SF). Back-brushing is MANDATORY when spraying penetrating stains. Paint is LEAST RECOMMENDED for wood fences — moisture-driven peeling risk requires mandatory risk warning documentation.

includes: Moisture content verification (MC <=19% untreated wood, <=25% PT pine — HARD STOP)
PT pine seasoning verification (3-6 month minimum — HARD STOP if <3 months)
Mill glaze removal sanding (new milled cedar only — 80-grit)
Pressure wash (1,000-1,500 PSI — lower than deck for vertical surfaces)
Mildew eradication treatment (conditional — when visible mildew present)
Previously coated surface sanding (80-100 grit for refinishing)
Chemical wood restoration for weathered fences (3-step: alkaline strip, acid brighten, rinse — 12-24 hr dry)
Stain-blocking primer (cedar + solid_stain/paint only — tannin bleed prevention)
Standard exterior primer (PT pine + paint only)
Stain application — transparent, semi-transparent, or solid (spray_backbrush, brush, roll)
Paint application — exterior acrylic latex (spray, brush, roll) — LEAST RECOMMENDED
Second coat application (solid_stain and paint only — penetrating stains are single-coat)
Both-sides application sequencing (side A -> equipment move -> side B)
Post and cap end-grain treatment (absorbs 2-3x face rate)
Gate hardware removal and reinstallation
Landscape protection along fence base (both sides, LF-based)
Hardscape protection for adjacent driveways/patios/walkways
Siding protection at fence-to-house tie-in
Neighbor-side overspray protection (spray method only)
Final walkthrough inspection and touch-up
Paint risk warning documentation (when coating_type = paint)

excludes.item: Metal fences (wrought iron, aluminum, chain link)
excludes.route_to: Future SF_METAL_EXT_v1 — different substrate, primer, and coating chemistry
Out of scope — maintenance-free by design

excludes.item: Fence construction, post setting, board replacement

excludes.route_to: PaintScope — applies multiplier before delivering final SF to spec

excludes.item: Environmental condition scheduling (wind, dew point, surface temp)
excludes.route_to: SOP process constraints — not estimatable at bid time

configuration_dimensions.description: PRIMARY configuration dimension — replaces quality_tier for this spec. Drives coating chemistry (penetrating vs film-forming), maintenance cycle, failure mode profile, primer requirement, and coat count.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Semi-transparent is the professional standard for residential wood fences (~55% of work). Transparent = economy/minimal (1-2 yr cycle). Solid_stain = enhanced durability (3-7 yr). Paint = longest theoretical cycle (5-10 yr) but LEAST RECOMMENDED — moisture-driven peeling risk. Paint triggers mandatory risk warning. No quality_tier dimension — coating_type drives everything.

configuration_dimensions.description: Drives prep module selection and prep material requirements. This spec covers both new construction AND existing fences.
configuration_dimensions.notes: New: seasoning verification (PT pine) + mill glaze sanding (cedar). Weathered: chemical restoration protocol (strip, brighten, rinse — 12-24 hr dry). Previously_coated: assess existing coating, sand/strip, recoat. Each condition has fundamentally different prep time and materials.

configuration_dimensions.description: Fence wood species. Drives prep chemistry, tannin management, primer requirements, and production rate modifier.
configuration_dimensions.notes: PT pine ~65% of residential fences (cost-driven). Cedar ~30% (premium aesthetic). Cedar requires tannin management (oxalic acid brightener) and tannin-blocking primer for solid stain/paint. PT pine requires 3-6 month seasoning verification. Composite, vinyl, metal explicitly excluded.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for stain/paint coats.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Spray_backbrush is production method for privacy and shadowbox fences (2-person crew: one sprays, one back-brushes). Back-brushing MANDATORY for penetrating stains — spray-only PROHIBITED. Brush is primary for split rail and detail. Roll for privacy fence flat panels. Paint spray does not require mandatory back-brush (film-forming).

paintable_items.name: Fence Field Surface (panels, boards, posts, rails, gates — both sides)
paintable_items.counting_rules: Net fence field surface area in square feet. PaintScope delivers FINAL SF after (LF x Height x 2) and fence_style geometric multiplier (privacy 1.0x, shadowbox 1.6x, picket 0.7x). Includes both sides, all panels, posts, gates, and rails. Spec receives and uses final SF as-is — does NOT compute geometry.
paintable_items.notes: Single paintable item. Simplest item model among exterior wood specs. Posts and gates are stained as part of the field pass, not separate line items. Post end-grain (tops) absorbs 2-3x face rate — accounted in material coverage profiles, not as separate item.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Net fence field surface area (both sides, after style multiplier)
Primary dimension — coating type (transparent, semi_transparent, solid_stain, paint)
Wood condition (new, weathered, previously_coated) — drives prep module selection
Fence style (privacy, shadowbox, picket, split_rail) — INFORMATIONAL to spec, PaintScope uses for geometric multiplier
Wood substrate (cedar, pressure_treated_pine) — drives tannin management and primer requirement

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of gates — drives hardware masking/removal tasks

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Linear feet of hardscape (walkway, driveway, patio) along fence line

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: When fence ties into house siding
required_paintscope_inputs.description: Siding area at fence-to-house junction requiring protection

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: When vehicles are parked near fence spray zone
required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of vehicles requiring full cover protection from overspray

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: When spraying fence side facing neighbor property
required_paintscope_inputs.description: Linear feet of neighbor property line requiring protection
Boolean flag for new construction context — used with wood_condition

valid_input_states.notes: SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD = new wood (cedar or PT pine). SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI = previously stained with penetrating stain. SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID = previously stained with solid stain. SS_EXT_WEATHERED = UV-degraded grayed wood. Wood_condition dimension maps: new -> SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD, previously_coated -> SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI or SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID, weathered -> SS_EXT_WEATHERED.

output_state.notes: Output state varies by coating_type. Transparent and semi-transparent both output SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI (penetrating finishes). Solid stain outputs SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID (film-forming). Paint outputs SS_EXT_PAINTED_SATIN.

protection_zones_required.notes: Landscaping, mulch beds, ground cover along fence base on BOTH sides. Drop cloth/plastic along fence line at ground level. Primary overspray and drip zone. Extends 2-3 ft from fence base (4-6 ft for spray_backbrush). Stain drips onto vegetation are difficult to remediate.

Walkways, driveways, patios running along fence line. Stain on concrete is extremely difficult to remove — critical protection zone. Canvas for crew traffic areas (non-slip), plastic for non-traffic areas.
House siding where fence attaches to structure. Tape and plastic at fence-to-house junction. Upgrade to full plastic coverage (4-6 ft up siding face) when spraying.
Vehicles parked near fence being sprayed. Full cover with plastic sheeting. Overspray drift onto vehicles is a liability risk. Conditional — only when vehicles are within spray range.

Neighbor's landscaping, structures, and items near fence. Drop cloth along neighbor's side of fence base. Wind drift is primary concern. Coordinate with neighbor before deploying protection. Only activated for spray_backbrush method.

material_systems_summary.name: Clear / Transparent Wood Sealer
material_systems_summary.notes: Penetrating clear water repellent with UV filter. No color pigment. Wood grain fully visible. 1-2 year maintenance cycle. No primer required.

material_systems_summary.name: Semi-Transparent Penetrating Stain
material_systems_summary.notes: PROFESSIONAL STANDARD for wood fences. Pigmented penetrating stain — wood grain visible through color. 2-4 year cycle. No primer required.

material_systems_summary.name: Solid Color Fence Stain
material_systems_summary.notes: Film-forming solid body stain. Complete grain masking. 3-7 year cycle. Tannin-blocking primer required on cedar.

material_systems_summary.name: Exterior Latex Paint (LEAST RECOMMENDED)
material_systems_summary.notes: LEAST RECOMMENDED for wood fences. Moisture-driven peeling risk. High-permeability formulation critical. Mandatory risk warning. Primer required on all substrates.

material_systems_summary.name: Alkyd Stain-Blocking Primer
material_systems_summary.notes: MANDATORY on cedar + solid_stain/paint. Prevents tannin bleed through film-forming coatings. Also serves as standard exterior primer for paint on PT pine.

material_systems_summary.name: Fence Cleaner / Stripper (Alkaline)
material_systems_summary.notes: First step in chemical restoration. Alkaline wood cleaner/stripper. MUST be neutralized with brightener before staining.

material_systems_summary.name: Wood Brightener (Oxalic / Citric Acid)
material_systems_summary.notes: Second step in chemical restoration. Neutralizes alkaline stripper, restores natural wood color. Oxalic acid preferred for cedar tannin management. Also used standalone on cedar for tannin treatment.

modules.notes: Moisture test, seasoning verify, mill glaze sand, pressure wash, mildew treat, refinish sand
3-step chemical restoration: strip, brighten, rinse + dwell times + dry verify
Coat 1 — primer (conditional) + 3 stain method variants + 3 paint method variants
Coat 2 — 3 stain method variants + 3 paint method variants
Final walkthrough + touch-up + gate hardware reinstall

factor_modifiers.notes: Applies to APPLICATION tasks only. Semi-transparent is baseline.
Applies to PREP tasks only. Application rates not affected — prep normalizes surface.
Applies to both prep and application tasks. Cedar is softer, absorbs more stain.

production_summary.notes: No FAC_EXT_ACCESS — all fence work is ground-level. Fence_style geometric multiplier handled by PaintScope before SF reaches spec. Max combined modifier 2.29x (paint 1.30 x previously_coated 1.60 x cedar 1.10) — well under 4.0x cap.

compatibility_rules.name: Paint risk warning mandatory
compatibility_rules.action: Document moisture-driven peeling risk warning in project record with customer acknowledgment. Paint is LEAST RECOMMENDED for wood fences — moisture migrates through fence from both sides and lifts film.

compatibility_rules.name: MC hard stop
compatibility_rules.action: HARD STOP — do not apply stain or paint. Retest after 24 hr dry period. Wet wood prevents proper stain penetration and causes coating failure.

compatibility_rules.name: PT pine seasoning hard stop
compatibility_rules.condition: wood_condition = new AND substrate_material = pressure_treated_pine AND age < 3 months
compatibility_rules.action: HARD STOP — do not stain. PT pine requires 3-6 month seasoning for preservative cure and MC reduction. Water bead test: if water beads on surface, wood is not ready.

compatibility_rules.name: Cedar tannin-blocking primer required for solid/paint
compatibility_rules.condition: substrate_material = cedar AND coating_type IN (solid_stain, paint)
compatibility_rules.action: Activate SYS_EXT_FNCE_PRIMER_STAIN_BLOCK. Cedar tannins bleed through film-forming coatings — primer is NOT optional on cedar with solid stain or paint.

compatibility_rules.name: Back-brushing mandatory for spray penetrating stains
compatibility_rules.condition: application_method = spray_backbrush AND coating_type IN (transparent, semi_transparent, solid_stain)
compatibility_rules.action: Spray-only is PROHIBITED for penetrating stains. Spray must be followed immediately by back-brushing to force stain into wood grain pores. 2-person crew required.

compatibility_rules.name: Chemical restoration requires separate mobilization
compatibility_rules.action: Chemical restoration (strip + brighten + rinse) requires 12-24 hr dry time before staining. Plan for separate mobilization day. Shorter than deck (24-48 hr) due to vertical drainage.

compatibility_rules.name: Penetrating stains skip primer entirely
compatibility_rules.action: Do NOT apply primer. Primer seals wood surface and prevents stain penetration. Penetrating stains must absorb directly into wood fibers.

compatibility_rules.name: Transparent not recommended for PT pine
compatibility_rules.action: Warn customer — greenish PT chemical color shows through clear sealer. Semi-transparent recommended instead for PT pine to add color over green tint.

round_configurations.name: Transparent Stain — 1 Coat
round_configurations.notes: Single coat penetrating transparent sealer. No primer. No second coat. Simplest configuration.

round_configurations.name: Semi-Transparent Stain — 1 Coat
round_configurations.notes: Single coat semi-transparent penetrating stain. Professional standard default. No primer. No interstage.

round_configurations.name: Solid Stain — 2 Coats (+ Optional Primer on Cedar)
round_configurations.notes: Two-coat solid stain. Cedar adds tannin-blocking primer (3 applied layers total). No formal interstage — allow full dry between coats per TDS (4-24 hr).

round_configurations.name: Paint — Primer + 2 Coats
round_configurations.notes: LEAST RECOMMENDED. Primer mandatory (tannin-blocking on cedar, standard exterior on PT pine). 2 finish coats. 3 applied layers total. Full dry between coats. Document risk warning.

variants.notes: Most common residential job. New PT pine, semi-transparent spray_backbrush. Single coat. Full neighbor-side protection for spray.
Premium new cedar fence. Semi-transparent spray_backbrush. Single coat. No primer (penetrating stain).
Small fence or split rail. Brush application. Minimal protection (no spray overspray).
Solid stain on cedar — tannin-blocking primer + 2 coats. Full protection suite.
Solid stain on PT pine — no primer needed. 2 coats.
LEAST RECOMMENDED. Paint on cedar — tannin-blocking primer + 2 paint coats. Full protection. Mandatory risk warning.
LEAST RECOMMENDED. Paint on PT pine — standard exterior primer + 2 paint coats. Mandatory risk warning.
Common maintenance refinish. Weathered cedar — chemical restoration required (separate mobilization). Single coat semi-transparent after restoration.
Economy option — clear sealer on new cedar. Natural wood appearance. 1-2 year maintenance cycle. Fastest application.

maintenance_cycles.notes: Shortest cycle. Annual recoat typical. Minimal UV protection — wood will gray if cycle is missed. Simple re-apply without stripping (penetrating product).
Professional standard cycle. Clean and recoat — no stripping needed. Penetrating stain erodes gradually. Sun-exposed faces (south/west) need maintenance sooner.
Longer cycle on vertical surfaces (no foot traffic wear). May need sanding or partial strip if peeling at recoat time. Film-forming product — more prep for maintenance than penetrating stain.

Longest theoretical cycle but HIGHEST FAILURE RISK on fences. Moisture-driven peeling often starts within 2-3 years on weather-exposed face. Maintenance recoat requires scraping, sanding, priming bare spots, and repainting. Most expensive maintenance cycle.

risk_flags.name: Paint on wood fence — moisture-driven peeling
risk_flags.description: Paint forms a film that traps moisture migrating through fence wood from both sides. Fences are fully exposed to weather on BOTH faces — unlike walls where one side is protected. Moisture trapped under paint film causes blistering, peeling, and premature failure within 2-3 years on weather side.
risk_flags.mitigation: Use penetrating stains instead (transparent, semi-transparent). If paint is specified: use HIGH PERMEABILITY formulation, document risk warning with customer acknowledgment, use 100% acrylic for maximum flexibility.

risk_flags.name: PT pine seasoning — premature stain failure
risk_flags.description: New PT pine saturated with waterborne preservatives (ACQ, CA-B, MCA). Stain applied before 3-month seasoning fails to penetrate — blotchy appearance, complete failure within first season. Most common fence staining callback.
risk_flags.mitigation: HARD STOP: verify PT pine age >= 3 months. Water bead test. MC < 19%. Schedule later if wood is too new.

risk_flags.name: Cedar tannin bleed through film-forming coatings
risk_flags.description: Cedar contains water-soluble extractive tannins that bleed through solid stain and paint, causing dark brown/red discoloration. Most severe with water-based coatings and at end-grain (board tops).
risk_flags.mitigation: Tannin-blocking primer (alkyd/shellac-based) is MANDATORY for solid stain and paint on cedar. For penetrating stains, some tannin bleed is acceptable. Oxalic acid brightener pre-treatment dissolves surface tannins.

risk_flags.name: Overstaining — excess product buildup
risk_flags.description: Too much penetrating stain creates a tacky surface film that does not cure properly, attracts dirt, and peels. Common when back-brushing is skipped (spray pooling in board joints).
risk_flags.mitigation: Back-brush thoroughly. Thin coats. No pooling at board joints or bottom edges. Wipe excess from non-absorbing surfaces.

risk_flags.name: Shadowbox fence spray access difficulty
risk_flags.description: Shadowbox fences (alternating boards on opposite sides) create corrugated profile requiring spray from both sides with angle adjustments. May reduce effective production rate below baseline 215 SF/hr.
risk_flags.mitigation: PaintScope geometric multiplier (1.6x) accounts for surface area. Estimator should note potential rate reduction for complex shadowbox profiles.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: House siding at fence-to-house tie-in point. Different coating system. Protection required at junction.
Posts are integral to fence system — stained as part of field pass, same coating.
Gates stained with fence field — same coating. Hardware removal/reinstall is separate task.
Ground/landscaping at fence base. Protection-only — not a painted surface.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Setup -> Prep -> Chemical Restore (weathered only) -> Apply Coat 1 (primer if applicable, then stain/paint) -> Apply Coat 2 (solid/paint only) -> Final Inspect -> Cleanup
sequencing_notes.both_sides_workflow: Side A protection -> Side A application -> Equipment move (~30-60 min) -> Side B protection -> Side B application. Both sides must complete coat 1 before either side gets coat 2.
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Landscape (both sides) -> Hardscape -> Siding tie -> Neighbor property (spray only) -> Gate hardware -> Coating work -> Protection teardown -> Equipment cleanup
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence_penetrating: Prep -> Apply stain coat 1 (both sides) -> Final inspect -> Touch-up -> Cleanup
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence_film_forming: Prep -> Primer (cedar+solid/paint or any+paint) -> Apply coat 1 (both sides) -> Dry 4-24 hr -> Apply coat 2 (both sides) -> Final inspect -> Touch-up -> Cleanup
sequencing_notes.chemical_restoration_sequence: Strip apply -> 15-20 min dwell -> Scrub -> Rinse -> Brighten apply -> 10-15 min dwell -> Rinse -> 12-24 hr dry -> MC verify -> Proceed to staining
sequencing_notes.key_prohibitions: NO spray-only for penetrating stains (back-brush mandatory). NO staining at MC > 19% (25% PT). NO staining PT pine < 3 months old. NO penetrating stain over primer. NO solid/paint on cedar without tannin-blocking primer.

cross_spec_boundaries.boundary: Metal fences (wrought iron, aluminum, chain link)
cross_spec_boundaries.notes: Different substrate, primer, and coating chemistry entirely. Not wood fence scope.
Post setting, board replacement, structural repair. Painting spec covers coating only.
Wind, dew point, surface temperature are scheduling/process concerns. Not estimatable at bid time.

relationships.notes: Shares stain-based architecture with deck spec (coating_type replaces quality_tier). Key departures from deck: vertical surface (faster drainage, different spray technique), both-sides application, no foot traffic, ground-level access only (no height modifier), shorter dry times after chemical restoration.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for exterior wood fence staining & painting. First stain-based exterior spec — coating_type replaces quality_tier as primary dimension. Key features: 4 coating types (transparent/semi_transparent/solid_stain/paint), 3 wood conditions (new/weathered/previously_coated), 2 substrates (cedar/PT pine), 3 application methods (spray_backbrush/brush/roll — spray-only prohibited), single paintable item (ITM_FENCE_FIELD SF), 35 tasks across 7 modules (incl. chemical restoration for weathered and coat 2 for film-forming), 7 material systems (2 stains + 1 sealer + 1 paint + 1 primer + 2 prep chemicals), 3 factor modifiers (coating_type/wood_condition/substrate_material), max stack 2.29x, 4 round configurations, 5 protection zones. Paint on fence is LEAST RECOMMENDED with mandatory risk warning. PT pine seasoning (3 months) and MC (19%) are hard stops. Cedar requires tannin-blocking primer for solid/paint. Fence_style multiplier handled by PaintScope. No height modifier — ground-level work.
